arxiv-1905-05854.title: On Structured Lyapunov Functions and Dissipativity in Interconnected LTI Systems
arxiv-1905-05854.creator: Andrej Jokić and Ivica Nakić
arxiv-1905-05854.description: A 2019 arXiv research paper by Andrej Jokić and Ivica Nakić. In this paper we study connections between structured storage or Lyapunov functions of a class of interconnected systems (dynamical networks) and dissipativity properties of the individual systems. We prove that if a dynamical network, composed as a set of linear time invariant (LTI) systems interconnected over an acyclic graph, admits an additive quadratic Lyapunov function, then the individual systems in the network are dissipative with respect to a (nonempty) set of interconnection neutral supply functions.

arxiv-2104-12124.title: On Measure Quantifiers in First-Order Arithmetic (Long Version) Thanks: Supported by ERC CoG “DIAPASoN”, GA 818616.
arxiv-2104-12124.creator: Melissa Antonelli, Ugo Dal Lago, Paolo Pistone
arxiv-2104-12124.description: Abstract We study the logic obtained by endowing the language of first-order arithmetic with second-order measure quantifiers. This new kind of quantification allows us to express that the argument formula is true in a certain portion of all possible interpretations of the quantified variable.

arxiv-2105-12778.title: Statistical Depth Meets Machine Learning: Kernel Mean Embeddings and Depth in Functional Data Analysis
arxiv-2105-12778.creator: George Wynne, Stanislav Nagy
arxiv-2105-12778.description: Abstract Statistical depth is the act of gauging how representative a point is compared to a reference probability measure. The depth allows introducing rankings and orderings to data living in multivariate, or function spaces. Though widely applied and with much experimental success, little theoretical progress has been made in analysing functional depths.

arxiv-2109-05477.title: Stylistic Retrieval-based Dialogue System with Unparallel Training Data
arxiv-2109-05477.creator: Hao Fu, Yan Wang, Ruihua Song, Tianran Hu, Jian-Yun Nie
arxiv-2109-05477.description: Abstract The ability of a dialog system to express consistent language style during conversations has a direct, positive impact on its usability and on user satisfaction. Although previous studies have demonstrated that style transfer is feasible with a large amount of parallel data, it is often impossible to collect such data for different styles.

arxiv-2209-05908.title: Monoidal Pull-Push II: Local Systems
arxiv-2209-05908.creator: Angus Rush
arxiv-2209-05908.description:

In topology, one often studies spaces via algebraic invariants associated to them. One such invariant of particular interest is the
n
th homology
of a space
X

is the abelian group consisting of formal sums of certain maps from the standard
n
-simplex
\Delta^{n}
into
X

n

arxiv-2305-03891.title: Many-body non-Hermitian skin effect under dynamic gauge coupling
arxiv-2305-03891.creator: Haowei Li, Haojie Wu, Wei Zheng, Wei Yi
arxiv-2305-03891.description: Abstract We study an atom-cavity hybrid system where fermionic atoms in a one-dimensional lattice are subject to a cavity-induced dynamic gauge potential. The gauge coupling leads to highly-degenerate steady states in which the fermions accumulate to one edge of the lattice under an open boundary condition.

arxiv-2408-04816.title: FUSE-ing Language Models: Zero-Shot Adapter Discovery for Prompt Optimization Across Tokenizers
arxiv-2408-04816.creator: Joshua Nathaniel Williams, J. Zico Kolter
arxiv-2408-04816.description: Abstract The widespread use of large language models has resulted in a multitude of tokenizers and embedding spaces, making knowledge transfer in prompt discovery tasks difficult. In this work, we propose FUSE (Flexible Unification of Semantic Embeddings) 1 1 1 https://github.com/jnwilliams/FUSE_prompt_inversion.

arxiv-2409-03188.title: Predefined-Time Distributed Non-convex Optimization via a Time-Base Generator Thanks: Submitted to the editors DATE.
arxiv-2409-03188.creator: Qinlong Lin, Yang Liu, Jianquan Lu, Weihua Gui
arxiv-2409-03188.description: Abstract In this paper, we propose two novel multi-agent systems for the resource allocation problems (RAPs) and consensus-based distributed optimization problems. Different from existing distributed optimal approaches, we propose the new time-base generators (TBGs) for predefined-time non-convex optimization. Leveraging the proposed time-base generator, we study the roughness and boundedness of Lyapunov function based on TBGs.

arxiv-2410-00653.title: Vector interaction bounds in NJL-like models from LQCD estimated curvature of the chiral crossover line
arxiv-2410-00653.creator: Mahammad Sabir Ali, Deeptak Biswas, Chowdhury Aminul Islam
arxiv-2410-00653.description: Abstract We obtain improved bounds on both the flavor-independent and -dependent vector interactions in a 2 + 1 2+1 -flavor Nambu–Jona-Lasinio (NJL) model using the latest precise LQCD results of the curvature coefficients of the chiral crossover line. We find that these lattice estimated curvature coefficients allow for both attractive and repulsive types of interactions in both the cases.

arxiv-2505-24788.title: Drop Dropout on Single-Epoch Language Model Pretraining
arxiv-2505-24788.creator: Houjun Liu * , John Bauer and Christopher D. Manning
arxiv-2505-24788.description: Abstract Originally, dropout was seen as a breakthrough regularization technique that reduced overfitting and improved performance in almost all applications of deep learning by reducing overfitting. Yet, single-epoch pretraining tasks common to modern LLMs yield minimal overfitting, leading to dropout not being used for large LLMs.

arxiv-2507-10958.title: Notebook for the eRisk Lab at CLEF 2025
arxiv-2507-10958.creator: Anthony Miyaguchi, David Guecha, Yuwen Chiu, Sidharth Gaur
arxiv-2507-10958.description: Abstract This Working Note summarizes the participation of the DS@GT team in two eRisk 2025 challenges. For the Pilot Task on conversational depression detection with large language-models (LLMs), we adopted a prompt-engineering strategy in which diverse LLMs conducted BDI-II-based assessments and produced structured JSON outputs. Because ground-truth labels were unavailable, we evaluated cross-model agreement and internal consistency.

arxiv-2509-23727.title: AudioMoG: Guiding Audio Generation with Mixture-of-Guidance
arxiv-2509-23727.creator: Junyou Wang, Zehua Chen, Binjie Yuan, Kaiwen Zheng, Chang Li Yuxuan Jiang Jun Zhu
arxiv-2509-23727.description: Abstract Guidance methods have demonstrated significant improvements in cross-modal audio generation, including text-to-audio (T2A) and video-to-audio (V2A) generation. The popularly adopted method, classifier-free guidance (CFG), steers generation by emphasizing condition alignment, enhancing fidelity but often at the cost of diversity.

pmc-11351924.title: An Interpretable System for Screening the Severity Level of Retinopathy in Premature Infants Using Deep Learning
pmc-11351924.creator: Wenhan Yang, Hao Zhou, Yun Zhang, Limei Sun, Li Huang, Songshan Li, Xiaoling Luo, Yili Jin, Wei Sun, Wenjia Yan, Jing Li, Jianxiang Deng, Zhi Xie, Yao He, Xiaoyan Ding, Paolo Zaffino, Andrea Cataldo, Maria Francesca Spadea
pmc-11351924.description: Accurate evaluation of retinopathy of prematurity (ROP) severity is vital for screening and proper treatment. Current deep-learning-based automated AI systems for assessing ROP severity do not follow clinical guidelines and are opaque. The aim of this study is to develop an interpretable AI system by mimicking the clinical screening process to determine ROP severity level.

This study aims to elucidate the mechanisms underlying the susceptibility of S. aureus to lugdunin by screening a transposon-based mutant library generated using the lugdunin-susceptible S. aureus strain HG001. pmc-12510441.title: Pericardial Tamponade in Trauma: A Systematic Review of Diagnosis, Emergency Management, and Surgical Outcomes
pmc-12510441.creator: Murhaf Assaf, Aya Abdalla, Amr Essam Shaltout, Shahzad Ahmad, Anwaar Ul Haq, Huba Ali Khan, Muhammad Faisal Saleem, Muhammad Nabeel Ahmad, Mohamed K Abouelsadat, Manahil Awan, Nadia Malik
pmc-12510441.description: Traumatic pericardial tamponade is a life-threatening emergency caused by the rapid accumulation of blood in the pericardial sac, leading to cardiac compression, decreased cardiac output, and obstructive shock. Early recognition and prompt intervention are crucial in preventing cardiovascular collapse. However, timely diagnosis remains challenging due to overlapping injuries and non-specific clinical signs in trauma settings.

pmc-12648445.title: Endobronchial Recurrence of Renal Cell Carcinoma 12 Years After Nephrectomy: A Rare Case Treated With Microwave Coagulation Therapy
pmc-12648445.creator: Hirofumi Nakano, Yukihiro Sugimoto, Ryota Aoki, Yu Tsukasa, Tetsurou Takeuti, Takayuki Yamamoto, Sosei Abe, Masanori Takayama
pmc-12648445.description: Endobronchial metastasis (EM) from renal cell carcinoma (RCC) is a rare manifestation of intrathoracic spread. RCC is known for its potential to recur long after nephrectomy, and EM may mimic primary lung cancer, complicating diagnosis and management. A 69-year-old male patient with a history of nephrectomy for RCC presented with progressive dyspnea.

pmc-12954698.title: Digital Health Interventions in Children and Adolescents With Type 1 Diabetes Mellitus and Their Impact on Clinical and Behavioral Outcomes: Scoping Review
pmc-12954698.creator: Eirena Beh, Jiaying Lin, Geraldyn Leong, Pei Yi Loh, Ee Jin Poh, Daniel Chan
pmc-12954698.description: BackgroundEffective self-management of type 1 diabetes mellitus (T1DM) by children and adolescents remains challenging despite advances in insulin delivery and glucose monitoring technologies. Mobile health (mHealth) interventions have emerged as promising tools to support pediatric diabetes care. However, their clinical impact and the behavioral mechanisms through which they operate—particularly those grounded in social cognitive theory (SCT)—are not well established.

pmc-13008730.title: Seafood not from the sea: examining consumer behavioral intentions toward plant-based seafood
pmc-13008730.creator: Min-Yen Chang, Ching-Tzu Chao, Jia-Hong Chen, Han-Shen Chen
pmc-13008730.description: The intensifying challenges of climate change and marine resource depletion have propelled plant-based seafood to become the forefront of sustainable food innovations. Although this sector has experienced remarkable technological advancements globally, empirical research on consumer acceptance, particularly in Taiwan, remains limited.
